messages.subject: Three-way mixed Procrustes ANOVA
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I got stuck in an analysis from a very complicated design. If the team could give me some hints, that will be great. I really appreciate your precious time.

In particular, I am conducting a research which needs a three-way (?) mixed Procrustes ANOVA analysis. After I read the thread “procD.lm and RRPP - how to disable model truncating” (between Mike and Tyler), I followed the suggestions, but I am still not very sure. I am wondering whether the team could help check the code I write below, based on my understanding of the code in that thread, to make sure I am on the right track.

Regarding the analysis, the outcome variable is 2-D coordinates (x, y). The predictors include one between-subjects variable, city (2 cities), and two within-subjects variables, pos (2 positions) and methods (3 different methods). Id would be treated a random effect, that is, those ids were sampled randomly. For one id, theoretically there are 6 sets of coordinates (2 cities by 3 methods), nested with one id. It is of main interest to investigate whether there is any significant difference in those 2-D coordinates between cities after accounting for Age, positions, methods, random effects from ids, and correlation among coordinates.

Here is a toy data set:

   id city Age pos method x_cor y_cor

   1   1   35    L   app1  -0.2  0.1

   1   1   35    L   app2  -0.6 -0.5

   1   1   35    L   app3   0.2  0.9

   1   1   35    R   app1   0.8  0.7

   1   1   35    R   app2   0.4  0.1

   1   1   35    R   app3   0.1  0.7

   2   0   25    L   app1   0.8  0.3

   2   0   25    L   app2  -0.3 -0.5

   2   0   25    L   app3   0.7  0.5

...

"Pos" and "method" are within-subjects factors, and are crossed so I would have 6 sets of (x,y) coordinates nested within each "id". "id" is treated as a random effect.

"City" is a between-subjects factor.

(x,y) coordinates have been processed using Generalized Procrustes Analysis with "gpagen".

My main research question is: is there any significant difference in the (x,y) coordinates between the two cities after accounting for Age, pos, methos, and random effect from id? Random effect from id is of no interest.

Here is the formula I created based on the thread mentioned previously:

 ***

fit1 <- procD.lm(coords ~ (id/(pos:method)) + city*pos*method + Age, RRPP = TRUE, print.progress = FALSE)

Is the formula correct? If not, what formula should I use?

Thanks again for your precious time.

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Three-way mixed Procrustes ANOVA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul, your set up looks to be appropriate to me. Hopefully you have enough observations that you don’t have a degrees of freedom issue to worry about.  You might also be careful about adjusting your anova error terms.  I would also use type III sums of squares instead of type I.  I think you want to make sure that when you’re evaluating your fixed effects, random effects are included in the null model. Therefore, you don’t want term order to have any impact.

Hope that helps!

Mike

messages.subject: Coloring tips in phylomorphospace3d
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am trying to color the terminals in a tree-dimensional phylomorphospace plot (function phylomorphospace3d), but I am not succeeding.

I have a phylogeny ("f.tree" object, phylo format) with 68 tips and 67 internal nodes, in addition to a set of landmarks which I used for a gm.prcomp() ("pca" object). I have already checked the match() between f.tree$tip.label and dimnames(pca$x)[[1]].

By running the command below, only the branches of the phylogeny were colored:
> phylomorphospace3d(f.tree,pca$x[,1:3],
                        control=list(ftype="off",
                                    col.edge=colors,
                                    lwd=2, spin=F))

I've tried to set "col.edge=colors" and "t.bg <http://t.bg>=colors" parameters, also applying "as.factor(colors)" to both of these scenarios. Finally, I modified the "colors" array to "length = 135" (corresponding to f.tree$Nnode + Ntip(f.tree)), setting "black" as the color for the internal nodes. Unfortunately, all these attempts have resulted in failure.

It seems I am missing something here. Does anyone have any idea about which attribute I am leaving out?

Thanks in advance.
Diego Almeida-Silva

messages.body_plain:
Diego,

You must be using an old version of geomorph. The function ‘phylomorphospace3d’ has long been deprecated.  It is now subsumed within the function gm.prcomp.

With that function, one can color the tip dots, but I just checked and found that for some reason, one cannot specify different colors for the branches. I am not sure why.

I can try to look for a solution but it might be a little while; I have quite a few things on my plate.

Best,

Dean

messages.subject: Issues with random effects in procD.lm
messages.subject_clean: Issues with random effects in procD.lm
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am having some issues with getting my procD.lm models to successfully run and give proper estimates. I am trying to test whether or not there is a difference between the shape of the left and right claws of crayfishes (each crayfish has 2 claws). Normally, I would do this in lme4 by testing (shape ~ claw.side + (1| crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id>)). Crayfish.id is the random effect that I want in my model. Each crayfish has two shape observations in my data set, one for the left claw and one for the right claw (i..e, the claw side variable).

I have tried multiple different syntax's trying to get the model to run, but each time the summary comes out with very strange (incorrect) estimates.

Below are some of the examples that I have tried, with the model summaries included.

model1<- procD.lm(coords~ csize + crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id> + claw.side/crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id>, data=agdt,RRPP=T,iter=9999)

summary(model1)
                                              Df      SS   MS     Rsq  F  Z Pr(>F)
claw.side                             1 0.00988    0 0.01660  0  0 0.5005
csize                                     1 0.03835    0 0.06441  0  0 0.5005
claw.side:crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id>       209 0.54707    0 0.91899  0  0 0.5005
Residuals                              0 0.00000 -Inf 0.00000
Total                                    211 0.59530

model2<- procD.lm(coords ~ claw.side/crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id>, data=agdt,RRPP=T,iter=9999)

summary(model2)
                                              Df      SS        MS    Rsq   F   Z Pr(>F)
claw.side                               1 0.00988 0.0098820 0.0166 NaN   0 1.0000
claw.side:crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id>          210 0.58542 0.0027877 0.9834 NaN NaN 0.9921
Residuals                              0 0.00000       NaN 0.0000
Total                                     211 0.59530

I believe that there are issues with how I am coding my random effect, because the models seem to run fine when I take out the crayfish.id <http://crayfish.id> variable. If anyone has any advice that would be great.

Thanks!
Zack

messages.body_plain:
Dear Dean,
Thanks for your reply!

I have checked here, and I am using the last stable version of geomorph available on CRAN (4.0.3). I am using gm.prcomp() to perform the PCA, but I had not tried using it to generate the phylomorphospace, actually.

I saw in vignettes an example of coloring tip dots by setting the attribute "bg" to the base function plot() on the output of gm.prcomp(). It works very well in my data, as follows:
> pca2<-gm.prcomp(A = gdf$coords, phy = gdf$phy)
> plot(pca2, time.plot = T, pch = 21, bg = colors, cex = 3,
                              phylo.par = list(edge.width = 1.5, tip.txt.cex = 0.75))

On the other hand, I did not find a way to set PC3 as a z-axis for the plot, instead of time...

Again, thank you so much for your attention, Dean. I would really appreciate if you could give me your inputs on that.

Best regards,
Diego

>
>

>
> With that function, one can color the tip dots, but I just checked and found that for some reason, one cannot specify different colors for the branches. I am not sure why.
>
>
>
> I can try to look for a solution but it might be a little while; I have quite a few things on my plate.
>
>
> Best,
>
>
>
> Dean

>
>
>
> Dear all,
>
> I am trying to color the terminals in a tree-dimensional phylomorphospace plot (function phylomorphospace3d), but I am not succeeding.
>
>
>
> I have a phylogeny ("f.tree" object, phylo format) with 68 tips and 67 internal nodes, in addition to a set of landmarks which I used for a gm.prcomp() ("pca" object). I have already checked the match() between f.tree$tip.label and dimnames(pca$x)[[1]].
>
>
>
> By running the command below, only the branches of the phylogeny were colored:
>
> > phylomorphospace3d(f.tree,pca$x[,1:3],
>                         control=list(ftype="off",
>                                     col.edge=colors,
>                                     lwd=2, spin=F))
>
>
>

Finally, I modified the "colors" array to "length = 135" (corresponding to f.tree$Nnode + Ntip(f.tree)), setting "black" as the color for the internal nodes. Unfortunately, all these attempts have resulted in failure.
>
> It seems I am missing something here. Does anyone have any idea about which attribute I am leaving out?
>
>
> Thanks in advance.
>
> Diego Almeida-Silva
